title: The Future We Choose
subtitle: Moving from one reality to another.

trails.title: Workshop Area
trails.description: The story begins with a melody that echoes through the airspace of the workshop, signaling the beginning of a new day.

content.speaker: Resident I
content.text: We should take these components to the appropriate comrade. With my years of experience in mining, I can assure you that they are still usable and will be put to good use.

content.speaker: Resident I
content.text: Maybe they contain traces of runium, explaining their pristine appearance. In these times of steel shortages, every little contribution counts ...

content.speaker: Resident II
content.text: I imagine Comrade Vila is with the children right now, making sure they don't miss their lessons.

content.speaker: Resident II
content.text: Could it be that the miners have returned to the abandoned mine? Maybe we should take the shorter route to the hotel and let Comrade Evgeni investigate.

content.speaker: Resident I
content.text: Shh, see those people walking in front of the hotel? Are they from Zeno? Let's not talk about them behind their backs.

content.speaker: Resident II
content.text: Yeah, I see them. Isn't Comrade Evgeni negotiating with Zeno? They must be looking for him.

content.speaker: Resident I
content.text: They left. It looks like Comrade Evgeni isn't there. We'll have to come back later.

content.speaker: Resident II
content.text: Tomorrow or the day after, perhaps.

content.speaker: Resident II
content.text: Honestly, this is not the way I want to leave this town.

content.speaker: Resident I
content.text: Ugh, I still have the scars from shoveling snow on my legs, and we just fixed the windows at home. Who wants to leave just like that?

content.speaker: Resident II
content.text: But what Comrade Evgeni said was reasonable, and he is always truthful ...

content.speaker: Resident I
content.text: You're afraid he'll hear you! We may be close to the meeting room, but—

content.speaker: Resident II
content.text: I'm not afraid, or I wouldn't have made the decision to come here. We weren't afraid in the pioneer days either. What Comrade Vila says is exactly what everyone said back then.

content.speaker: Resident II
content.text: The town has been built, and we have been living here for a while now. Our days are not as hectic as they used to be, but it is invigorating to see the resurgence of the pioneer spirit after such a long time!

content.speaker: Resident I
content.text: Hey, alright! That's the attitude we need! If we walk a little faster, we can still make it back to work on time!

items.text: Days Later
Children's Square, Rayashki

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Ms. Vila, they've been doing strange things.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Father took out a lot of old books, and he spends most of his time looking over his blueprints now. He said, "They will be the key to saving the town."

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Shame I can't read those books or help with anything.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: My dad was acting strange, too. He started fiddling with the bottles from under his bed again.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: But Mom didn't scold him this time. She even took out some of her treasures from the cabinet.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Reindeer horn, Noisy Birch sap, Golden-Teeth Seal whiskers.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Dad said his potions would keep everyone energetic for a whole day.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Even Mr. Miser took out his wand from the safe box!
The children cluster around Vila, pleading for answers.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Heh heh.
Vila is about to speak when hurried laboring footsteps interrupt her.

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: Move, kids.

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: Good luck, Comrade Vila.
Regrettably, his march cannot proceed.
As he's now become the children's newest focus.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Mr. Patrik.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Are you doing strange things, too?
The book bag on his shoulder cannot elude the children's scrutiny.
It is not a cookbook he carries, but something far weightier.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: How to Use and Maintain Model Э-050, Operation Manual of Model СК-1562 ...

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: These dusty books ... They look older than me!

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: Hahaha, these "old friends" are our textbooks.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Do adults take exams, too?

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: We're doing something far more important than exams, kids.

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: We haven't used these old fellas since Zeno brought the new ones. Most of our comrades don't know how to operate them.

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: Now is the time to put them back into use. Comrade Knut has been teaching us how to use these "outdated" technologies.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: That's right. All the adults have been divided into many groups.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Knut is leader of the engineering group, and Pasono's uncle is in the investigation group, while Nina's father has joined the potion group.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: All of them take part in the critter combat training at dusk every day, and we share our combat experience with each other.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: And everyone is working hard to explore the mine.
The children burst into questions, seeking the current whereabouts and activity of every single adult they can think of.

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: Haha! We will be able to live on our own without Zeno!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Ms. Vila, I want the town to be proud of me, too!

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Is there anything that we can do?

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: I have lots of metal toy trains. Can we make components out of them?

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: They can spin and whistle like a mine cart!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: That's a great idea. I'm sure it will inspire everyone.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: No! Let them use mine first!
Hands shoot up among the children, each a ready volunteer.

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: Calm down, children. I know you want to do your bit.

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: But our future needs you.

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: Now, your job is to study hard, so Rayashki can rely on you in the future.

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: Understand?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Oh. What about Avgust? We can't find him.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: He'll be so sad if he doesn't get to have a job too.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: *chuckles*

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Don't worry, Nina. He's helping the town in his own way.
Abandoned Mine, Rayashki

items.speaker: Kikituk
items.text: *roars*

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Ears!
A gunshot sounds, and a Kikituk swiftly scurries away.

items.speaker: Kikituk
items.text: *roars*

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Whiskers!
The boy is a conductor of a symphony of arms.
Gunfire and the noise of battle follow in the wake of the little sunflower's hands.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: It's only been a few months. Can't believe the monsters have already occupied the whole place.

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: Well, not a problem as long as we got our mischievous little comrade. He always knows exactly where they will come out.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Things wouldn't have gone nearly as smoothly without him.

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: I would never have believed he could do this if Comrade Windsong hadn't endorsed him.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: "Never underestimate any of our comrades, big or small." Do I need to repeat that again?
Of course, Avgust is securely guarded, despite his dangerous mission.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Well done, Avgust. You protected everyone.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Protected?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But I was just teaching our monster friends how to dance right. They are slow learners.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Yes, that's what we want you to do.
She struggles to match her words to her little friend's own imaginative interpretations.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: A performance with the Kikituks.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Your job is to tell which critter, emm, I mean, which friend, is dancing wrong.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: That's your talent, isn't it? Just like you showed us before!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Oh!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But, what if they dance right?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Mmm.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Then, they deserve some Alenka chocolate, don't they?
Indeed, for all those scattered, many more come slinking in behind them.
They shadow every move, intent on repelling their intruders.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Comrade Sergiyan, our new friend is right beside your boots. I think he is hoping to kiss them. Will you dance with him?

items.speaker: The Other Resident
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Watch out!
*zap*

items.speaker: The Other Resident
items.text: Ah!

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Back off!
Evgeni surges forward, white light piercing the last Kikituk's nostrils.
Evgeni pushes the carcass aside, allowing blood to drip onto the snow.
He fixes intently on Windsong.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: There are many more critters than we can deal with here.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Many of us are injured. We must retreat.
Faint moans rise from a stretcher, bandages and bloodstains accumulating in a small mound on the snow.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: We made the decision to come here together, Comrade Evgeni.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: We are so close to the depths. We must not give up now!

items.speaker: The Other Resident
items.text: Hiss, ah! I know everyone's wounded, but look how far we've gone. It's been worth it, don't you think?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: This is all my fault. I'm sorry.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Don't be, Comrade Windsong. You've given us a workable plan and helped us recognize our little comrade's potential, no?
He ruffles Avgust's head.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: He's only a child.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: He's one of us, Comrade Evgeni. I will keep him safe.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: We aren't just digging a mine now.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: If we manage to find this resource, no one will have to leave, and we can continue to live together, right?

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Hmph!
Scattered applause burst up like firecrackers, until it becomes a thundering display.
Rifles, refurbished and polished, rise in harmony with pickaxes and tools.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: These wounds are nothing compared to the glory of our future.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Again, I think this is a foolish idea.
He says nothing else, then turns to leave without looking back.
